sentences.text: Cutibacterium namnetense was described as a new species under the name Propionibacterium namnetense, from strains isolated from human bone and tissue samples.
Those strains are anaerobic, Gram-positive-staining pleomorphic rods most closely related to Propionibacterium acnes, from which whole genome comparison gave an OrthoANI value of 88.5 percent.
A review lists C. namnetense among five recognised Cutibacterium species, a genus created when skin propionibacteria isolates were transferred from the genus Propionibacterium.
A complete circular chromosome of 2.40 Mb was reported for a C. namnetense isolate from a Malaysian human acne sample.
MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry can misidentify C. namnetense and Cutibacterium modestum as Cutibacterium acnes.
